name: Condo Control
tagline: Property management platform for condo and HOA boards: resident portal, amenity bookings, visitor parking, package tracking, violations, and electronic owner voting.

pricing.basis: quoted per building, typically scaled by unit count
pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The web app itself is unremarkable: forms, a calendar, a document library, a notice board. What you cannot one-shot is the part that makes a board sign a contract, namely electronic owner meetings and voting that hold up under condo legislation, auditable records of notices and consents, and a vendor the property manager can point at when an owner disputes a quorum. Add the parts that touch the physical building: guard tour logs, package scanning, key fob and access control integrations, mass emergency call-out to hundreds of residents who never log in. A personal replacement also makes no sense here, since the user is a corporation with fiduciary duties, not a person. Build the amenity booking app for your own building if you want, just do not route a bylaw vote through it.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted building portal with announcements, amenity booking with conflict checks, maintenance requests, visitor parking passes, and a document library.
requirements: a small server or VPS and a domain
an SMTP provider for notification email
someone willing to onboard and support non technical residents forever
whatYouLose: Electronic owner meetings and voting with quorum tracking, proxies, and the paper trail an auditor or tribunal will ask for
Native mobile apps and push notifications, which is how residents actually receive anything
Emergency mass broadcast by email, SMS, and voice to an entire building
Security guard and concierge tooling: patrol logs, incident reports, package scanning, visitor logs
Access control, intercom, and accounting integrations, plus a support line the property manager can call at 2am
moatNotes: Boards buy indemnity and a named vendor as much as software. A volunteer treasurer's side project is a liability the insurer will ask about.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the buyer is a board that rotates every year and a property manager who runs twenty buildings, not a tinkerer. They need the same workflow in every building, a support contact, records that survive a disputed vote, and software that keeps working after the one technical owner sells their unit and moves out. The booking calendar is cheap; the continuity, the legal defensibility, and the guard-desk hardware side are not.
notes: The amenity calendar is a weekend; the owner vote is not. The moat is condo legislation plus the fact that a board cannot sign a contract with a hobby project.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted building portal for a single small condo or HOA. Residents book amenities, read notices, file maintenance requests, and issue visitor parking passes.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via Prisma, file at ./data/building.db
- Auth: email magic links only, via Nodemailer against SMTP credentials in .env. No OAuth, no passwords, no third party auth service.
- Deploys as one Node process behind a reverse proxy. No cloud services beyond SMTP.

Data model:
- Unit (number, floor), Resident (name, email, unitId, role: owner | tenant | admin)
- Amenity (name, description, slotMinutes, openHour, closeHour, maxActiveBookingsPerUnit)
- Booking (amenityId, unitId, start, end, status)
- Notice (title, body markdown, pinned, publishedAt)
- Request (unitId, category, description, photos, status: new | in_progress | done, internal notes)
- VisitorPass (unitId, plate, visitorName, validFrom, validTo)
- Document (title, file path, category, uploadedAt)

Features that must work:
- Amenity booking with server side conflict checks, per unit booking caps, blackout dates set by admin, and cancellation.
- Admin console for residents, units, amenities, blackout dates, and request triage.
- Notice board with pinned items and an email digest sent on publish to all verified residents.
- Maintenance requests with image upload to local disk, status changes, and email on status change.
- Visitor parking passes with a printable pass page and an admin list of active plates by date.
- A read-only document library with upload restricted to admins.

Explicitly out of scope, do not build stubs for these: electronic owner voting, proxies, quorum tracking, SMS or voice broadcast, access control or intercom integrations, accounting or dues collection, payments, native mobile apps, analytics or telemetry.

Seed the database with 12 units, 2 amenities (party room, gym), and 3 sample notices. Include a README covering .env variables (SMTP_HOST, SMTP_USER, SMTP_PASS, MAIL_FROM, APP_URL), first admin bootstrap, and a one command sqlite backup. Mobile first layout, plain and legible, no animation.
